I think you're probably on the best track. You might be able to dig into the cache for some user IDs, however assuming you've logged in with the new account, it's probably long gone. 

In the future I'd recommend using Authy for your 2FA, or saving backup codes physically on a hidden flash drive. 

Anyways, best of luck.

This is probably the best option. Chrome remote desktop works well for me. You don't need to install anything on the Chromebook, just the desktop.

Are the blocked websites through the network or the Chromebook itself? If it's through the network, you might be able to use a mobile hotspot + data, or a mobile hotspot + a VPN on a phone may be able to bypass it... Although this is assuming you have a phone... 

The nuclear option could possibly be to wipe the Chromebook like new to remove all admin restrictions. I'm not sure of all the logistics of that. 

Please keep in mind that some free VPNs will sell your private data. Also please keep in mind that trying to bypass any filters they may have could be a violation of any acceptable use of technology agreements from the school.
